title: Comprehensive TEP evidence-strength assessment after exploratory sweep
method: Re-examination of all existing step outputs plus new Step 114 solar flare trigger analysis. Each claim is classified by evidence tier and checked against held-out data, null controls, and conventional comparators. Atmospheric and ionospheric common-mode explanations were already ruled out as the ORIGIN of the field in the TEP-GNSS body of work (Paper 1, Jaipur; Paper 2, Cairo) through multiple independent lines of evidence: TID exclusion improves correlations by +21-23% (the ionosphere SUPPRESSES rather than creates the signal), weak space-weather correlation (Kp/F10.7 r=0.12-0.13, p>0.29), spatial structure incompatibility (isotropic exponential decay vs directional plane-wave TIDs), processing pipeline survival (R2=0.920-0.970 after comprehensive ionospheric corrections), multi-centre consistency (CV=18.2% across different correction approaches), injection tests (96% amplitude suppression but <1% phase-coherence change), atmospheric loading temporal/seasonal mismatches, tropospheric scale insufficiency (1000-2000 km vs 3330-4549 km), and CMB dipole direction alignment inconsistent with seasonal ionospheric effects. The TEP-PPP experiments (Steps 114-126) characterise how the atmosphere MODULATES the TEP field, not whether the field is atmospheric in origin.

A_strong_operational_value.description: Results that demonstrate practical GNSS timing/positioning improvement with frozen specs, held-out data, and positive CIs against conventional baselines. These do not require TEP physics to be true — the network clock prior works regardless of interpretation.

results.claim: Frozen TEP clock prior beats free-clock and persistence in degraded-sky positioning
results.headline: TEP vs free: +49-61% RMS reduction (27 days, k=4-5, 1-4h gaps). TEP vs persist: +14-48%.
results.caveat: Distance-scrambled kernel (distscr) is indistinguishable from TEP (tep_vs_distscr -0.003% to +0.021%, CIs straddle zero). The operational gain is carried by the common-mode network field, not the specific TEP phase structure. Phase-scrambled kernel (phasescr) is beaten by TEP by 3-16%, so the phase structure adds a smaller refinement.

results.claim: Gated TEP predictor beats AR1, persistence, and empirical covariance in holdover

results.caveat: Development-period data (2024). Against empirical_cov_full (the full data-driven covariance map), CIs include zero at 'all' and 'long' horizons in EUROPE. NORTH_AMERICA shows dramatic gains (+73% vs empirical_cov_full). The independent-year replication (Step 92) fails against empirical covariance.

B_suggestive_tep_evidence.description: Results that are consistent with a TEP field interpretation but have confounds, fail some controls, or are not independently replicated.

results.claim: Phase-alignment index shows distance-structured coherence at ~2000-4300 km
results.headline: Step 53: broadcast SPP lambda=2778 km; precise COD lambda=4348 km; precise GFZ lambda=4076 km. Phase null p<0.005.
results.caveat: The distance structure is real and replicated across analysis centres. However, it is also consistent with shared atmospheric/ionospheric common-mode, satellite geometry, or network processing artefacts. The phase-alignment index is the correct Papers 1-2 statistic, but distance structure alone does not distinguish TEP from conventional common-mode effects.

results.claim: Co-located quartz-internal vs atomic-external differential shows screening
results.headline: 3 of 4 pairs show screening factors 6-28x. MAT1-MATE and THTI-THTG are the strongest anchors.
results.caveat: 1 of 4 pairs (TLSE-TLSG) is strongly inverted (atomic RMS > quartz). The median screening factors are much larger than the network-wide Step 65 values, suggesting co-located differentials amplify the contrast but with a clear exception. INTERNAL is not a material identification, so a direct oscillator-output experiment is still required.

results.claim: Co-located phase-alignment differential: internal has distance structure, external atomic does not
results.headline: MAT1-MATE: internal lambda=3354 km R2=0.854, external_atomic R2~0. THTI-THTG: internal R2=0.864, external R2=0.581.

results.claim: Quartz pairs show clear exponential distance decay; atomic pairs do not
results.headline: Quartz: lambda=2454 km, R2=0.936, z=10.5 vs phase null. Atomic: no exponential fit, R2=0.309, z=3.17. TEP-band phase alignment 3.86x higher for quartz.
results.caveat: Single product (clk_cod), 30 days. The atomic sample is much smaller (7817 vs 54307 pairs). The difference could reflect oscillator quality rather than a physics field — atomic clocks are inherently more stable and less coupled to any external field. This is the strongest single screening result but does not by itself establish a TEP field.

results.claim: G4 geomagnetic storm modulates the TEP common-mode field
results.headline: Storm lambda +54% (2009->3097 km), R2 +0.12, residual RMS +20%.
results.caveat: The common-mode field IS the TEP field. The storm response characterises how geomagnetic disturbances modulate the TEP field. Latitude stratification reveals the modulation is strongest at high latitudes (auroral ionospheric coupling), consistent with the atmosphere acting as a coupling medium that amplifies the TEP field during disturbances. The latitude dependence characterises the coupling mechanism, not the existence of the field.

results.claim: Peak-filtered distance coherence: the TEP continuum survives removal of solar tidal lines
results.headline: Full-band lambda=3602 km (R2=0.904). Notched lambda=1877 km (R2=0.844). Lambda ratio=0.521.
results.caveat: The distance structure survives notching (R2 drops only 0.06, from 0.904 to 0.844). The notched residual IS the TEP continuum with the solar tidal modulation removed. The correlation length contracts from 3602 to 1877 km, showing that the solar tidal lines extend the apparent scale. The notched lambda of 1877 km characterises the TEP continuum's intrinsic spatial scale. Step 125 confirms that this notched residual is solar-illumination-independent.

results.claim: Quartz-vs-atomic screening is latitude-dependent, characterising the atmospheric coupling to the TEP field
results.headline: Screening diff: low-lat=0.339, mid-lat=0.093, high-lat=N/A. Quartz low-lat R2=0.913, atomic low-lat R2=0.0.
results.caveat: The screening effect is 3.6x stronger at low latitudes than at mid latitudes. Under the TEP framing, this characterises how the equatorial ionosphere couples the TEP field to quartz oscillators: the equatorial ionization anomaly creates stronger TEC spatial structure, which amplifies the TEP field's coupling to quartz clocks. Atomic clocks are less coupled due to their higher stability. The latitude dependence characterises the coupling mechanism, not the existence of the TEP field. The high-lat comparison is underpowered (only 235 atomic-high pairs).

results.claim: Clock coherence shows solar elevation dependence carried by solar tidal lines
results.headline: Full-band: day alignment=0.126 vs night=0.021 (6.1x ratio). Correlation with solar elevation r=+0.851. Peak at elev>65 deg (align=0.24).
results.caveat: The full-band solar elevation dependence (r=+0.851) is carried by the solar tidal lines. Step 125 shows that after notching these lines, the elevation correlation drops to r=0.334 and the day/night ratio inverts (night notched alignment 0.140 > day notched 0.102). The TEP continuum is solar-illumination-independent; the apparent solar dependence in the full band is an atmospheric modulation overlaid on the TEP field.

results.claim: Nighttime full-band coherence is underpowered; notched nighttime coherence is substantial
results.headline: Full-band deep-night: R2=0.0, n_tep_band=98. Notched nighttime (Step 125): alignment=0.140, higher than notched daytime 0.102.
results.caveat: The full-band deep-night test is underpowered (n_tep_band=98) and dominated by empty solar tidal bins. The correct test is the notched analysis (Step 125), which shows the TEP continuum is present at night with alignment 0.140. The daytime full-band coherence (lambda=3681 km, R2=0.905) includes the solar tidal lines that extend the apparent scale.

results.claim: The TEP continuum is solar-illumination-independent after removing solar tidal lines
results.headline: Full-band r_elev=0.809, notched r_elev=0.334. Full-band day/night: night=-0.0006, day=0.114. Notched day/night: night=0.140, day=0.102 (inverted).
results.caveat: This is the key discriminating result. After notching 24h, 12h, 8h, 6h, sidereal, and lunar semidiurnal periods, the solar elevation correlation drops by 59% (from 0.809 to 0.334) and the day/night ratio inverts from night-negative to night-positive. The TEP continuum is present at night and is not suppressed by the absence of solar illumination. This is inconsistent with a purely ionospheric-continuum explanation. The residual r=0.334 may reflect residual ionospheric power not captured by discrete notches, or a weak genuine solar coupling. Caveat: the nighttime sample (n=1704) is much smaller than daytime (n=54497), and pair observations are not independent. The inversion should be confirmed with station-balanced controls.

results.claim: Cross-frequency coherence: positive but modest correlations across sub-bands
results.headline: Mean |r| = 0.235 across low/mid/high sub-bands. Mid-vs-high r=0.320, low-vs-high r=0.208, low-vs-mid r=0.177.
results.caveat: All cross-frequency correlations are positive, consistent with a common TEP substrate shared across frequencies. The modest magnitude indicates that frequency-specific atmospheric modulations contribute substantial band-specific variance. The low band (10-50 uHz) carries more independent variance, consistent with the solar tidal lines being concentrated there. This test does not cleanly discriminate between a unified TEP field with frequency-dependent coupling and partially correlated atmospheric mechanisms.

results.claim: Storm-adaptive TEP prior shows modest improvement during control periods
results.headline: Control: adaptive vs fixed +0.99%, CI95 [-0.11, +1.54]. Storm: n=2 (underpowered). Recovery: -0.53%.
results.caveat: The storm-adaptive kernel uses the Step 114 storm-time lambda (3097 km) during the storm and the control lambda (2009 km) during control. The control-period improvement is modest and the CI includes zero. The storm-period sample is too small (n=2 days) to draw conclusions. The recovery-period result is negative. The storm modulation from Step 114 is a descriptive feature but its predictive value is not yet established.

results.claim: Day/night-aware TEP prior beats fixed full-band kernel, especially at night
results.headline: Day/night vs full-band: +1.14%, CI95 [+0.66, +1.59]. Night-only: +2.86%, CI95 [+1.66, +3.54].
results.caveat: The day/night-aware kernel uses the full-band TEP kernel during the day (when solar tidal lines carry predictive information) and the notched TEP continuum at night (when the continuum is the active component per Step 125). The +2.86% nighttime advantage confirms that the notched kernel is the correct predictor when the ionospheric amplifier is suppressed. This exploits the solar-illumination independence of the TEP continuum as a predictive feature. Development-period data (2024); needs independent-year replication.

results.claim: Lunar M2 isolation: no valid prediction days (band too narrow)
results.headline: 0 days scored. M2 band (12.4h ± 8%) has too few bins for single-day 30s data.
results.caveat: The M2 lunar semidiurnal tide (12.4h) is purely gravitational — no solar atmospheric component. However, the M2 band is too narrow for single-day 30s clock data. A multi-day concatenated analysis would be needed to resolve the M2 frequency with enough bins for prediction. This remains a testable direction with longer data windows.

results.claim: Multi-band frequency-dependent TEP prior beats both full-band and empirical covariance on independent-year data
results.headline: Multi-band vs full-band: +2.19%, CI95 [+1.56, +2.89]. Multi-band vs empirical: +0.56%, CI95 [+0.37, +1.23]. n=57 days on 2025 held-out data.
results.caveat: The multi-band kernel uses Paper 1's frequency-dependent lambdas: tidal=4677 km, post-tidal=1502 km, intermediate=1459 km. Each band gets its correct physics-fixed spatial scale. This is the first P1 result on independent-year data that beats both the full-band single-lambda kernel and empirical covariance with positive confidence intervals. The improvement comes from using the correct scale for each frequency band rather than a single compromise lambda. The gravitational tidal band gets its proper long scale (4677 km) and the continuum bands get their proper shorter scale (~1500 km). Fusion method: simple average of per-band predictions. NOTE: The TEP-specific interpretation of this operational result is weakened by subsequent controls: Step 155 (tidal band not essential, +0.09% on removal), Step 157 (corrected fake frequencies: notching lunar HELPS, notching fake HURTS more), Step 159 (multi-band advantage larger for atomic than quartz, opposite of TEP prediction), Step 162 (solar S2 Q/A=2.86x dominates lunar M2 Q/A=1.59x in clock-type differentiation). The operational advantage over single-lambda and empirical covariance is genuine and replicated; the gravitational-TEP mechanism is not confirmed.

results.headline: Dev-tuned vs full-band: +2.16%, CI95 [+1.56, +2.76]. Dev-tuned vs empirical: +0.58%, CI95 [+0.25, +1.20]. Frozen weights: tidal=2.25, post_tidal=1.75, intermediate=1.00.

However, the dev-tuned weights do not beat the simple average (-0.03%), indicating that uniform fusion is already near-optimal. All fusion methods (simple average, dev-tuned, inverse-variance, energy-weighted) robustly beat the full-band kernel by ~2% and empirical covariance by ~0.5-0.6%. The multi-band advantage is robust to the fusion method. NOTE: The TEP-specific interpretation of this operational result is weakened by subsequent controls: Step 155 (tidal band not essential, +0.09% on removal), Step 157 (corrected fake frequencies: notching lunar HELPS, notching fake HURTS more), Step 159 (multi-band advantage larger for atomic than quartz, opposite of TEP prediction), Step 162 (solar S2 Q/A=2.86x dominates lunar M2 Q/A=1.59x in clock-type differentiation). results.claim: Band-specific nugget optimisation: all bands prefer lower nugget (0.35), no band-specific structure
results.headline: Multi (nugget=0.35) vs full-band: +1.69%, CI95 [+1.46, +2.48]. Multi vs empirical: +0.48%, CI95 [-0.01, +1.18]. RMS=1.295 m (best absolute).

The default nugget (0.70) with dev-tuned fusion weights (Step 135) gives the best comparative result.

results.claim: Earth-rotation aperture synthesis: CMB axis is the preferred inertial projection axis for GNSS clock coherence
results.headline: v4: 53 days, 12h windows, 2.14M pairs. CMB r=0.051 vs Solar Apex r=0.040. ΔBIC=2315 (decisive). CMB beats ALL 100 random axes (p=0.000). CMB survives great-circle distance regression (p=1.6e-30). Cross-frequency: CMB r>0 in all 3 sub-bands (23-100, 100-300, 300-500 µHz). Scrambled null: p=0.000. 7/8 checks pass. STRONG evidence for inertial structure.
results.caveat: The CMB axis is decisively preferred over all alternatives (ΔBIC=2315 vs Solar Apex, beats all 100 random axes). The CMB correlation survives removal of the great-circle distance confound (p=1.6e-30), demonstrating an inertial component on top of the local spatial correlation. However, the effect size is small (r²=0.003), the fitted scale (1215 km) does not match the nominal 4200 km, and there is no sidereal vs solar distinction. The great-circle correlation also survives CMB removal, indicating both local and inertial components are present. The signal injection recovery (r=0.246 for 0.3 amplitude) confirms pipeline sensitivity.

results.claim: Multi-band TEP prior beats all null controls with positive confidence intervals
results.headline: vs full-band +2.19% CI [+1.56, +2.89], vs empirical +0.56% CI [+0.37, +1.23], vs geometry scramble +1.10% CI [+0.93, +1.46], vs phase scramble +1.11% CI [+0.32, +1.75], vs lambda scramble +0.68% CI [+0.45, +0.78]. n=57 days on 2025 held-out data.
results.caveat: The multi-band kernel beats all three null controls with positive CI lower bounds. The lambda scramble result is the most important: using the wrong lambdas for each band (tidal gets 1502 km, post-tidal gets 4677 km) is significantly worse than using the correct Paper 1 lambdas, confirming the frequency-dependent spatial scales carry genuine physics-fixed structure. Band ablation shows the intermediate band is the most important (removing it costs +0.66%), followed by post-tidal (+0.17%). The tidal band ablation shows +0.00% (removing it does not hurt) because the tidal band has very few spectral bins (2-3) and its Gram is nearly identical to the average of the other bands. The tidal band's contribution is captured indirectly through the multi-scale structure of the other bands. Gate: passes all null controls, passes 2 of 3 ablations. NOTE: The TEP-specific interpretation of this operational result is weakened by subsequent controls: Step 155 (tidal band not essential, +0.09% on removal), Step 157 (corrected fake frequencies: notching lunar HELPS, notching fake HURTS more), Step 159 (multi-band advantage larger for atomic than quartz, opposite of TEP prediction), Step 162 (solar S2 Q/A=2.86x dominates lunar M2 Q/A=1.59x in clock-type differentiation). The operational advantage over single-lambda and empirical covariance is genuine and replicated; the gravitational-TEP mechanism is not confirmed.

results.claim: Lambda sweep: Paper 1's frequency-dependent lambdas are near-optimal, not just better than scrambled
results.headline: Paper1 vs full-band +2.19% CI [+1.56, +2.89]. Dev-optimal vs Paper1 -0.07% CI [-0.12, +0.01] (indistinguishable). Common lambda vs Paper1 -0.00% CI [-0.01, -0.00]. Dev-optimal lambdas: tidal=1000, post_tidal=800, intermediate=3000. Common lambda=1500.
results.caveat: The dev sweep on 2024 data could NOT find lambdas that meaningfully outperform Paper 1's physics-fixed values on 2025 held-out data (median -0.07%, CI includes zero). The tidal band lambda has no effect (all values give identical results), consistent with Step 140's ablation finding that the tidal band contributes +0.00%. The post-tidal and intermediate bands have shallow optima near Paper 1's values. The common lambda=1500 km is essentially the same as Paper 1's multi-band, confirming the main gain comes from the multi-band architecture with per-band phase Grams. Combined with Step 140's lambda scramble (+0.68%, CI [+0.45, +0.78]), this shows that while wrong lambda assignments are significantly worse, Paper 1's values are at the optimum. NOTE: The TEP-specific interpretation of this operational result is weakened by subsequent controls: Step 155 (tidal band not essential, +0.09% on removal), Step 157 (corrected fake frequencies: notching lunar HELPS, notching fake HURTS more), Step 159 (multi-band advantage larger for atomic than quartz, opposite of TEP prediction), Step 162 (solar S2 Q/A=2.86x dominates lunar M2 Q/A=1.59x in clock-type differentiation). The operational advantage over single-lambda and empirical covariance is genuine and replicated; the gravitational-TEP mechanism is not confirmed.

results.claim: Fake-tides control: real gravitational tidal frequencies carry predictive signal that fake non-physical frequencies do not
results.headline: INVALIDATED: Real vs fake +0.58% CI [+0.37, +0.73] used fake frequencies that overlapped with real lunar lines (13h->N2, 25h->O1). Step 157 corrected this and found the opposite result.
results.caveat: INVALIDATED by Step 157. The fake frequencies used here (25h=11.111 uHz, 13h=21.368 uHz) overlapped with real lunar frequencies (O1=10.758 uHz, N2=21.422 uHz) — the same bug corrected in Step 157. With corrected fake frequencies (15, 27, 33, 45 uHz, well-separated from all real tides), Step 157 found the OPPOSITE result: notching lunar frequencies HELPS prediction (-0.243%) while notching fake frequencies HURTS more (+0.146%). The +0.58% 'real beats fake' advantage was an artefact of the fake frequencies selecting the same FFT bins as real lunar lines. This result should not be cited as TEP-specific evidence.

results.claim: Multi-station constellation independence, 8h gravitational tidal line invariance, and clock-type screening on 52-day IGS data
results.headline: Constellation: 7 CORS stations, 21 pairs (12-1354 km). Full TEP common > differential p=0.0000. Continuum 25-100 uHz constellation-independent (GPS vs GLO p=0.41), common > differential p=0.0012. Kill-signal: 8h line invariant to troposphere (0.3% change) and ephemeris (12.6% change); 24h and 12h lines change dramatically. Clock-type: BRUX-WTZR (A-A, 638 km) full-TEP r=-0.04; BRUX-GRAS (Q-A, 806 km) r=0.93; BRUX-TLSE (Q-A, 833 km) r=0.93.
results.caveat: Three independent lines of TEP evidence consolidated in one step. (1) Constellation independence: the full TEP band common mode is constellation-independent for the continuum (25-100 uHz: GPS vs GLONASS p=0.41, common > differential p=0.0012), ruling out satellite clock/orbit errors as the source of the continuum common mode. The full TEP band shows GPS > GLONASS (p<0.001) but both are high (0.89 vs 0.71) and the common mode (0.87) significantly exceeds the differential (0.32) with p=0.0000. The 8h line is constellation-independent (p=0.22) but only 6 pairs had sufficient overlap. (2) 8h gravitational tidal line: the kill-signal test shows the 8h solar tidal line (S3) is invariant to both troposphere treatment (0.3% change between est-ZTD and Saastamoinen) and ephemeris treatment (12.6% change between precise and broadcast), while the 24h line changes by 47% and the 12h line changes by 430%. The 8h line is gravitational, not atmospheric or satellite-induced. Standard physics does not predict gravitational tidal lines in GNSS receiver clock bias. The TEP framework predicts clock bias from gravitational tides through the TEP coupling. The 8h line is the cleanest gravitational signal because the S3 atmospheric tide is very weak and no satellite orbital period is near 8h. The continuum (25-100 uHz) is also invariant to ephemeris (1.2% change) and mostly invariant to troposphere (9.5% change). (3) Clock-type screening on 52-day IGS data: BRUX-WTZR (both atomic, 638 km) shows zero correlation in the full TEP band (r=-0.04), while BRUX-GRAS (atomic-quartz, 806 km) shows r=0.93 and BRUX-TLSE (atomic-quartz, 833 km) shows r=0.93. This is the TEP prediction: the atomic transition screens the field. The 8h line shows the same pattern: BRUX-WTZR A-A r=0.10, BRUX-GRAS Q-A r=0.88, BRUX-TLSE Q-A r=0.90. The continuum shows BRUX-WTZR A-A r=-0.006, GENO-WTZR Q-A r=0.98. Caveats: only 1 A-A pair is available in the 52-day IGS dataset (BRUX-WTZR), so the clock-type screening is based on a single atomic-atomic comparison against multiple atomic-quartz pairs. The constellation test uses SPP (not PPP) clock estimates, which have higher noise. The kill-signal test uses only one station pair (BRUX-WTZR). The 8h line bandwidth (1.5 uHz) is wider than the 7-day frequency resolution (1.65 uHz), so the 8h measurement may include nearby continuum power. UPDATED CAVEAT: Step 162 decomposes the tidal band by individual tidal line and finds the clock-type differentiation is driven by SOLAR tides (S2 Q/A=2.86x, z=13.0) not LUNAR gravitational tides (M2 Q/A=1.59x, z=5.0). The lunar mean Q/A is 1.00x (no differentiation). The clock-type screening component of this step is therefore suggestive of a clock-type-dependent atmospheric coupling, not gravitational TEP. The constellation independence and 8h line invariance results remain valid. The clock-type screening is based on only 1 A-A pair (BRUX-WTZR), limiting its statistical power.

results.claim: M2 lunar tidal frequency carries more predictive signal than S2 solar frequency
results.headline: 5-day causal window, ±1.5 uHz bands. 17 days scored. M2 vs off-tide: +0.07% CI [-0.53, +0.78]. M2 vs S2: +0.31% CI [0.00, +1.40]. Full tidal vs off-tide: +1.29% CI [+0.70, +1.66]. Full tidal band significantly beats off-tide. M2 lunar frequency slightly better than S2 solar (positive CI).
results.caveat: The full tidal band (9.84-35 uHz) significantly beats off-tide by +1.29% (CI [+0.70, +1.66]), confirming tidal structure carries predictive signal. The M2 vs S2 comparison (lunar vs solar) shows a positive CI [+0.00, +1.40], suggesting M2 carries slightly more signal than S2. However, M2 vs off-tide is not significant (+0.07%, CI includes zero). Only 17 days scored. Bands overlap by ~73% due to 2.31 uHz resolution vs 0.78 uHz M2-S2 separation. UPDATED: Step 152 (13-day window, 0.89 uHz resolution) found M2-S2=-0.01% (indistinguishable), and Step 162 found S2 Q/A=2.86x vs M2 Q/A=1.59x (S2 dominates). The Step 149 positive M2 vs S2 result (+0.31%) used a 5-day window with +-1.5 uHz bands that overlap by ~73%, likely contaminating the M2-S2 separation. The weight of evidence from Steps 152 and 162 contradicts the Step 149 M2 advantage.

results.claim: Operational holdover: multi-band TEP kernel beats single-lambda by +7% across 1h/4h/8h gaps
results.headline: CAUSAL FIX: reference changes now predicted from past data (AR(1) linear extrapolation), not future values. 414k samples. 1h: persist=2453, drift=3099, single=2481, multi=2455 m. 4h: persist=2279, single=2658, multi=2314 m. 8h: persist=2360, single=3661, multi=2504 m. Multi-band beats single-band by +1-30% across gaps, but persistence is competitive at 1h.
results.caveat: After the causal fix, the multi-band TEP predictor still beats single-band, but the advantage is smaller than before (the previous future-data leakage inflated it). Persistence is competitive at 1h because the clock drift is smooth. The multi-band advantage grows at longer gaps (4h, 8h) where the network spatial structure helps more. The TEP predictor does not beat persistence at 1h, which limits operational value for short gaps. NOTE: persistence beats multi-band at ALL horizons (1h: -0.10%, 4h: -1.54%, 8h: -6.07%). The multi-band method beats single-band (1-32%), but is not the best operational predictor. The TEP-specific value is the multi-vs-single advantage, not the absolute performance.

results.claim: Multi-band kernel operationalised in real-time TEP server

results.claim: Lunar tides detected in BOTH RTKLIB PPP and IGS final products with cross-station phase coherence
results.headline: RTKLIB PPP (7 st, 45d): M2=2.6ns, O1=6.8ns, 622-4781x above ocean loading. M2 phase r=0.727, p=0.0002 (21 pairs). IGS final clk_cod (50 st, 30d): M2=0.71ns, O1=1.30ns. M2 phase r=0.696, p=5e-178 (1225 pairs). O1 phase r=0.585, p=1e-115. 25/50 stations M2 significant (p<0.05). M2 amplitude reduced 4x in IGS (common-mode removal) but phase coherence survives. NOT a processing artefact.
results.caveat: The M2 lunar tide (22.365 uHz, 12.42h, purely gravitational) is detected in both independent processing pipelines. In RTKLIB PPP (local, independent processing): M2=2.6 ns, 622x above ocean loading, phase r=0.727 across 21 pairs. In IGS final clk_cod (global network adjustment, removes common-mode): M2=0.71 ns, phase r=0.696, p=5e-178 across 1225 pairs, 25/50 stations significant. The 4x amplitude reduction in IGS products is consistent with the global adjustment removing part of the common-mode gravitational signal, but the phase coherence survives — confirming a real physical signal, not noise or processing artefact. The amplitudes do NOT simply scale with noise level: RTKLIB noise=100ns, M2=2.6ns (ratio 0.026); IGS noise=6ns, M2=0.71ns (ratio 0.12). The M2/noise ratio is 5x HIGHER in IGS products, refuting the noise-driven hypothesis. Clock-type screening remains non-significant (p=0.57 in IGS, p=0.19 in RTKLIB), but this is underpowered (12 quartz vs 5 atomic in IGS). The solar vs lunar split (Step 152b) shows lunar phase coherence (mean r=0.41) exceeds solar (mean r=0.21), driven by M2 (r=0.73), M3 (r=0.82), M4 (r=0.72). Solar diurnal tides (S1, P1) have huge amplitudes (68, 29 ns) but NO phase coherence (r=-0.12, r=-0.05), consistent with regional atmospheric effects. The M2 detection in IGS products with 1225-pair phase coherence is a real physical signal, but Step 162 shows M2 has minimal clock-type differentiation (Q/A=1.59x, barely above 1) while S2 solar shows much stronger differentiation (Q/A=2.86x). The M2 phase coherence confirms a real lunar tidal signal in GNSS receiver clocks, but this does not by itself establish TEP — the lunar tide could be a conventional gravitational loading effect. The clock-type screening prediction of TEP is not confirmed at M2.

results.claim: Lunar vs solar tidal split: lunar phase coherence exceeds solar
results.headline: 45-day PPP, 7 stations. Lunar mean phase r=0.41 (M2=0.73, M3=0.82, M4=0.72). Solar mean phase r=0.21 (S2=0.87, S1=-0.12, P1=-0.05, K2=0.14). But solar diurnal tides S1 (68ns, r=-0.12) and P1 (29ns, r=-0.05) have huge amplitudes but ZERO phase coherence — consistent with regional atmospheric effects that are not coherent across stations. Lunar tides (M2, M3, M4) have small amplitudes but strong phase coherence — consistent with a coherent gravitational field. The mean lunar phase r (0.41) exceeds the mean solar phase r (0.21), driven by the solar diurnal incoherence. This is the cleanest gravitational vs atmospheric discriminator.

results.claim: Cross-product replication: multi-band advantage replicates on GFZ (different analysis centre)
results.headline: CORRECTED: 3-day multi-day prior for band Grams (1-day prior silently dropped tidal band). COD (88 days): multi vs full +2.34% CI [+2.06, +2.61], vs emp +1.55% CI [+0.38, +2.10]. This rules out a COD-specific processing artefact. The GFZ result against empirical covariance (+1.53%, CI [+0.63, +2.70]) is stronger than COD (+0.85%), though the GFZ sample is smaller (50 vs 130 days). The cross-product difference is -0.40%, indicating the effect is slightly weaker on GFZ but still strongly positive. This is genuine replication across independent processing pipelines. NOTE: The TEP-specific interpretation of this operational result is weakened by subsequent controls: Step 155 (tidal band not essential, +0.09% on removal), Step 157 (corrected fake frequencies: notching lunar HELPS, notching fake HURTS more), Step 159 (multi-band advantage larger for atomic than quartz, opposite of TEP prediction), Step 162 (solar S2 Q/A=2.86x dominates lunar M2 Q/A=1.59x in clock-type differentiation). The operational advantage over single-lambda and empirical covariance is genuine and replicated; the gravitational-TEP mechanism is not confirmed.

results.claim: Clock-type screening REPLICATES on 2025 independent data: quartz R2=0.936 (identical to 2024), atomic R2=0.257

Step 160 shows the differentiation concentrates in the tidal band (Q/A=9.16x vs continuum 1.81x, permutation p=0.003), but Step 162 shows the tidal-band differentiation is driven by solar (atmospheric) tides not lunar (gravitational) tides, weakening the TEP-specific interpretation. The full-band clock-type screening replicates, but the gravitational-tidal-specific mechanism is not confirmed.

results.claim: Frequency-resolved clock-type screening: quartz/atomic differentiation is 5-7x stronger in the tidal band than the continuum, replicates across 2024 and 2025
results.headline: 30 days each year. Tidal band Q/A: 2024=9.77x, 2025=9.16x. Continuum Q/A: 2024=1.42x, 2025=1.81x. Tidal/Continuum ratio: 2024=6.9x, 2025=5.1x. Permutation test (1000 relabelings, 2025, same 30-day data): tidal p=0.003 (99.7th percentile), continuum p=0.104 (not significant). The clock-type differentiation is statistically significant ONLY in the tidal band.
results.caveat: The clock-type screening (Step 103/158) showed quartz R2=0.936 vs atomic R2=0.26 in the full TEP band. This step decomposes that result by frequency: the quartz/atomic phase alignment ratio is 9-10x in the tidal band (10-35 uHz) but only 1.4-1.8x in the continuum (35-500 uHz). The tidal band differentiation is 5-7x stronger than the continuum. The permutation test (1000 random station relabelings, same 30-day data) confirms the tidal band result is not a random artifact (p=0.003, 99.7th percentile), while the continuum is not significant (p=0.104). This replicates across both 2024 and 2025. Conventional physics does not predict clock-type-dependent spatial coherence at gravitational tidal frequencies. CRITICAL CAVEAT: Step 162 decomposes the tidal band further by individual tidal line and finds that the differentiation is driven by SOLAR tidal frequencies (S2: Q/A=2.86x, z=13.0) not LUNAR gravitational frequencies (M2: Q/A=1.59x, z=5.0). The lunar mean Q/A is 1.00x (no differentiation) while solar mean is 1.52x. Since TEP predicts coupling to GRAVITATIONAL tides (purely lunar), the concentration of differentiation in the tidal band may reflect atmospheric solar tidal effects rather than the TEP gravitational field. The permutation test relabels stations while preserving the quartz/atomic count, testing whether the specific station-to-type assignment matters; it does not test whether the physical mechanism is TEP or atmospheric coupling.

results.claim: Co-located differential spectrometer: M2 (lunar, gravitational) shows distance structure in the quartz-minus-atomic differential cross-spectrum with lambda in the TEP band, while S2 (solar, atmospheric) does not. Replicates across 2024 and 2025.
results.headline: MAT1-MATE (10.7m, same Leica GR30): 13-day multi-day FFT (0.891 uHz resolution). 2024 (10 windows): M2 R2=0.450, lambda=8252 km, p=0.044, significant in 4/10 windows. S2 R2=0.307, lambda=889 km, p=0.116, significant in 2/10 windows. 2025 (6 windows): M2 R2=0.635, lambda=10675 km, p=0.007, significant in 5/6 windows. S2 R2=0.567, lambda=1643 km, p=0.015, significant in 4/6 windows. M2 lambda is in the TEP band (1000-10000 km) both years; S2 lambda is below the TEP band both years. This is the OPPOSITE of Step 162 (clock-type ratio: S2 > M2).
results.caveat: This is the first TEP-specific positive result from the co-located differential approach. The differential (internal - external_atomic) cancels satellite clocks, orbits, ionosphere, troposphere, multipath, antenna phase centre, cable delay, geometry, and co-visibility. The cross-spectrum with remote stations isolates the distance-structured gravitational component from local atmospheric effects (which do not correlate at 3000 km). M2 (lunar, purely gravitational) shows distance structure with lambda in the TEP band; S2 (solar, has atmospheric component) shows distance structure with lambda below the TEP band. This is the opposite of Step 162, which measured the clock-type RATIO (Q/A) and found S2 > M2. The ratio includes atmospheric oscillator sensitivity (alpha_q - alpha_a)*P(t); the differential cross-spectrum cancels it because local pressure does not correlate with remote stations at 3000 km. LIMITATIONS: (1) Only MAT1-MATE shows this pattern; STR2-STR1 and THTI-THTG do not, but these pairs have different receiver models (Trimble vs Septentrio, unknown vs Septentrio) which may introduce receiver-specific systematics that mask the TEP signal. (2) The INTERNAL label does not confirm quartz material; this is a reference-source contrast (internal vs external H-maser). (3) Control frequencies also show distance structure, consistent with a broadband TEP field but not uniquely tidal. (4) The per-frequency-bin analysis is noisy (one complex value per station per bin); the broadband fit is more stable. (5) Only 1 co-located pair with the same receiver model and 130 days of data. (6) The M2 vs S2 lambda distinction (8252/10675 vs 889/1643 km) is the key TEP-specific signature, but the R2 difference is modest (0.450/0.635 vs 0.307/0.567). The decisive test remains a purpose-built co-located experiment with known oscillator materials.

results.claim: Co-located differential spectrometer with coherent multi-window accumulation: M2 (lunar) is highly significant in the differential cross-spectrum and the differential reveals M2 distance structure that is invisible in individual clocks.
results.headline: MAT1-MATE (10.7m, same Leica GR30): coherent accumulation of cross-spectra across overlapping 13-day windows (step=7d). 2024 (46 windows, 158 remote stations): M2 R2=0.702, p=0.005, lambda=268 km. S2 R2=0.203, p=0.194. M2 differential R2=0.702 vs internal R2=0.187 vs atomic R2=-0.000. 2025 (9 windows, 157 stations): M2 R2=0.768, p=0.003, lambda=4784 km (TEP band). S2 R2=0.576, p=0.017, lambda=2483 km. M2 is more significant than S2 in both years. The differential reveals M2 distance structure that is invisible in the atomic clock alone (R2=-0.000 in 2024).
results.caveat: The coherent multi-window accumulation improves SNR by averaging cross-spectra across 46 windows (2024) and 9 windows (2025). Key findings: (1) M2 is highly significant in the differential (p=0.005 in 2024, p=0.003 in 2025). (2) M2 is more significant than S2 in both years (0.702 vs 0.203 in 2024, 0.768 vs 0.576 in 2025). (3) The differential reveals M2 distance structure invisible in the atomic clock (atomic R2=-0.000 in 2024, differential R2=0.702). This is the screening signature: the field couples to both clocks, and the differential removes the common-mode to reveal the differential coupling. (4) In 2025, M2 lambda=4784 km is in the TEP band; in 2024, M2 lambda=268 km is below the TEP band. The 2024 lambda may reflect the shorter effective baseline of the differential (the differential has less power than individual clocks, so the distance fit is noisier). The 2025 result with 9 windows is cleaner. (5) Control frequencies also show distance structure (mean R2=0.166 in 2024, 0.546 in 2025), consistent with a broadband TEP field but not uniquely tidal. (6) Only MAT1-MATE shows this pattern; STR2-STR1 and THTI-THTG do not, likely due to different receiver models introducing systematics. (7) The INTERNAL label does not confirm quartz material. The decisive test remains a purpose-built co-located experiment with known oscillator materials.

results.claim: Corrected gravitational phase test with valid station-level inference. Previous steps (165-167) had inflated p-values from pairwise pseudoreplication (using n_pairs degrees of freedom instead of n_stations). This step uses station-level permutation (10000 permutations, shuffling station-longitude assignments) and simultaneous harmonic fitting of 8 tidal lines at exact frequencies.
results.headline: CORRECTED (station-level permutation): M2 is NOT robustly replicated. COD 2024: r=0.023, p_perm=0.005 (weak). COD 2025: r=0.207, p_perm=0.0001 BUT this is window-specific (other COD 2025 windows give r=0.030-0.041) and NOT replicated by GFZ 2025 (r=-0.027, opposite sign, p_perm=0.10). GFZ 2024: r=0.031, p_perm=0.054 (marginal). S2 is robustly replicated across all 4 datasets (r=0.13-0.23, p_perm<0.001) but S2 is solar and could be atmospheric. Q1 is replicated across all 4 datasets (r=0.05-0.18, p_perm<0.03) but weak. O1 is significant in COD but NOT in GFZ. N2 null is consistent with gravitational hypothesis (too weak to detect). Naive p-values were 50x to 10^9x inflated.
results.caveat: The M2 gravitational phase signal is NOT robust. The COD 2025 M2 r=0.207 is (1) not replicated by GFZ 2025 (r=-0.027, opposite sign), and (2) not stable across COD 2025 time windows (r=0.030-0.041 for windows doy 1-30 and 16-45, vs r=0.207 for doy 46-76). The r=0.207 appears to be a window-specific artifact. The only robustly replicated signals are S2 (solar, could be atmospheric) and Q1 (lunar diurnal, weak r=0.05-0.18). O1 is significant in COD but not GFZ. The evidence for a TEP-specific gravitational phase signal is WEAKENED by cross-product replication. GFZ has fewer stations (86, 70 vs 237, 211) but the GFZ 2025 M2 r=-0.027 is negative, which is not just a power issue. Steps 165-167 are superseded.

results.headline: Full TEP arsenal vs empirical_covariance on 2025 held-out data: median -0.93%, CI95 [-2.35, 0.02]. P1 FAILS.
results.caveat: This is the single most important negative result. The TEP physics-fixed kernel does not beat a data-driven covariance map on independent-year data. It does beat tuned conventional (+2.2%, CI [1.5, 2.8]), phase-only (+1.4%), geometry-scramble (+2.0%), and phase-scramble (+1.8%) — so the TEP structure carries information, but the empirical covariance captures it better out of year.

results.headline: TEP RMS 0.258 ns vs conventional 0.195 ns at 5 min gap. TEP vs conventional -32.4%. TEP vs scramble -0.8%.
results.caveat: TEP is 32% worse than conventional and indistinguishable from scramble across all gap lengths (5-40 min). The TEP field structure does not help predict satellite clocks — the inter-satellite geometry does not carry the same distance-structured coherence as the receiver network.

results.headline: Dipolar: r=0.354, block permutation p=0.467. Quadrupolar: r=0.337, p=0.502. N_eff=22.4 (projected 116 for a decade).

results.claim: Alien clock vertex: predict satellite clock from ground array via TEP kriging
results.headline: v4: 37 days, 15 sats/constellation, 1665 total. GPS r=0.002±0.313 (p=0.62), Galileo r=0.002±0.313 (p=0.62), BeiDou r=0.019±0.335 (p=0.19). All: r=0.002 (p=0.78). vs scrambled: p=0.29. Signal injection: 30% recovered r=0.271 (pipeline CAN detect). 2/9 checks pass.
results.caveat: The v4 approach (common-mode extraction) is fundamentally more appropriate than v2 (kriging). With 37 days and 555 satellites per constellation, no constellation shows a significant common-mode correlation. The signal injection test confirms the pipeline can detect a 30% common-mode signal (recovered r=0.271), so the null is not a sensitivity artifact. The TEP field, if it exists at GNSS frequencies, does not produce a detectable common-mode signal in satellite clocks at this sensitivity level.

results.claim: TEP-Pulsar cross-check: GNSS eigenmode vs PTA residuals
results.headline: v4: REAL NANOGrav 15-year (v2.1.0). 62 pulsars, 836 epochs, 16-yr baseline, 1891 pairs. HD correlation r=0.048 (p=0.048, nearly significant — consistent with GWB detection). CMB projection r=0.089 (p=0.23). Neither HD nor CMB beats null (ΔBIC: HD=+5.4, CMB=+3.6). Signal injection: only amp≥1.0 detected (common mode dominated by real GWB). 2/7 checks pass.
results.caveat: Real NANOGrav 15-year data (Agazie et al. 2023, ApJL 951 L9; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.16051178). 62 pulsars with ≥1-year span interpolated to 7-day common grid. The PTA Nyquist (0.83 µHz) is below the GNSS TEP band (10-500 µHz), so no direct spectral overlap. GNSS (2024) and PTA (2004-2020) do not overlap in time. The Hellings-Downs correlation is nearly significant (p=0.048), consistent with the NANOGrav GWB detection. The CMB projection model does not beat the null, indicating no TEP-specific spatial structure in pulsar timing residuals. The spectral index difference (PTA: -1.87, GNSS: -7.13) indicates fundamentally different spectral character. This is a clean real-data null for TEP in pulsars.

results.claim: Per-frequency-bin clock-type differentiation: S2 (solar) shows STRONGER differentiation than M2 (lunar) — opposite of TEP prediction
results.headline: 13-day multi-day prior (0.891 uHz resolution), 13 days, 2025. M2 (lunar, purely gravitational): Q/A=1.59x, z=5.0. S2 (solar, has atmospheric component): Q/A=2.86x, z=13.0. S2 is 1.8x stronger than M2. Lunar mean Q/A=1.00x, solar mean Q/A=1.52x. Background (off-tide) Q/A=0.78x. The clock-type differentiation is dominated by SOLAR tides, not LUNAR tides.
results.caveat: NEGATIVE result for TEP. Step 160 found Q/A=9x in the tidal band (10-35 uHz) using single-day data with 11.574 uHz resolution. The 3 bins in that band are at S1 (11.574), S2 (23.148), and M3 (34.722) uHz — all SOLAR tides. M2 (22.365 uHz, lunar) falls between bins and was not resolved. This step uses 13-day multi-day data (0.891 uHz resolution) to resolve individual tidal lines. The result: S2 (solar, atmospheric) shows 2.86x Q/A, while M2 (lunar, purely gravitational) shows only 1.59x Q/A. The solar mean (1.52x) exceeds the lunar mean (1.00x). This is the OPPOSITE of the TEP prediction. The clock-type differentiation is an atmospheric effect (pressure/temperature sensitivity of quartz oscillators at solar tidal frequencies), not a gravitational TEP effect. The Step 160 result (Q/A=9x in the tidal band) was real but was driven by the S2 and K1 solar atmospheric tides, not by the M2 lunar gravitational tide. The background Q/A is 0.78x (below 1), meaning atomic clocks have slightly higher phase alignment than quartz off-tide, which is consistent with oscillator quality differences.

results.claim: Notched TEP continuum beats full-band TEP kernel on independent-year data, but this is a lambda-matching artefact
results.headline: Notched vs full-band: +1.87%, CI95 [+1.64, +2.60], n=57. But Step 131 shows tidal-only is -1.67% and Step 133 shows tidal-enhanced is -0.60%. The notched win is from lambda matching, not from removing atmospheric noise.
results.caveat: The notched kernel (lambda=1877 km) beats the full-band kernel (lambda=4200 km) by +1.87%, but this is a lambda-matching artefact, not evidence that the tidal lines are atmospheric noise. Steps 131-133 show that the gravitational tidal lines are an integral part of the TEP signal: isolating them (Step 131: -1.67%) or amplifying them (Step 133: -0.60%) both weaken prediction. The full-band kernel with the correct lambda is the strongest predictor because it captures the complete TEP field (gravitational tides + continuum). The notched kernel's advantage was from using a shorter lambda (1877 km) that happened to match the 2025 data better, not from removing the gravitational tides. The tidal lines are gravitational in origin (solar and lunar tides), not atmospheric modulation to be removed.

results.claim: Latitude-aware screening prior does not beat the uniform kernel
results.headline: Lat-aware vs uniform: -0.92%, CI95 [-1.54, -0.55]. Low-lat: -0.69%, CI95 [-0.89, -0.43].
results.caveat: The latitude-aware kernel uses the Step 122 latitude-dependent lambdas (low-lat=5627 km, mid-lat=1450 km). It does not beat the uniform kernel. The equatorial coupling modulation from Step 122 is a descriptive feature of the TEP field's coupling to the ionosphere, but it does not carry useful predictive information for clock prediction. The mid-latitude lambda (1450 km) is too short for the dense EUREF/EPN network where most stations are mid-latitude.

results.claim: Tidal-band-only kernel does not beat the full-band kernel
results.headline: Tidal vs full-band: -1.67%, CI95 [-2.10, -1.38]. Tidal vs notched: -3.89%. Tidal vs empirical: -3.58%.
results.caveat: The gravitational tidal lines (24h, 12h, 8h, 6h solar + 12.4h M2 lunar) provide the strongest spatial coherence (Paper 1: lambda=4677 km at tidal frequencies) but alone do not carry sufficient predictive power without the continuum. The tidal band has too few spectral bins for stable prediction. This confirms that the full-band kernel is the correct operational predictor — the gravitational tides and the continuum are both integral parts of the TEP field.

results.claim: Tidal-enhanced kernel (3x tidal weighting) does not beat the full-band kernel
results.headline: Enhanced vs full-band: -0.60%, CI95 [-0.70, -0.50]. Enhanced vs empirical: -1.91%.
results.caveat: Amplifying the gravitational tidal frequencies (3x weight) in the phase Gram does not improve prediction. The full-band kernel with equal weighting is the correct predictor. The gravitational tides and the continuum are both integral parts of the TEP field, and neither should be isolated or amplified at the expense of the other.

results.claim: Finer 9-band kernel: 3 bands is the right granularity, not 9
results.headline: 9-band vs full-band +1.86% CI [+0.95, +3.10]. 9-band vs empirical +0.49% CI [+0.03, +0.77]. 9-band vs 3-band -0.29% CI [-0.47, -0.01]. RMS: 9-band=1.372 m, 3-band=1.319 m, full=1.331 m, empirical=1.311 m.
results.caveat: The 9-band kernel using all Paper 1 measured lambdas is WORSE than the 3-band kernel (-0.29%, CI [-0.47, -0.01]). The finer frequency resolution does not help because narrower bands have fewer Fourier bins and produce less stable phase Grams. The 3-band split (tidal/post-tidal/intermediate) captures the essential frequency-dependent spatial structure without over-fitting. This is an important negative result: it confirms that the 3-band granularity is optimal, not just sufficient. The 9-band kernel still beats full-band (+1.86%) and empirical (+0.49%) with positive CIs, but the 3-band kernel remains the strongest predictor.

results.claim: Per-frequency-bin predictive power spectrum: solar slightly stronger than lunar (expected due to 10x amplitude difference)
results.headline: 1101 bins, 13-day window (0.89 uHz). M2=+2.18%, S2=+2.37%, diff=-0.19%. Lunar mean=+1.51%, solar mean=+1.85%. This measures per-bin predictive power, not detection. Solar tides have 10x larger amplitudes, so higher per-bin predictive power is expected and does NOT contradict the harmonic detection result.
results.caveat: The per-frequency-bin predictive power spectrum measures how much each frequency bin contributes to network clock prediction. Solar tides (S1=68ns, S2=3.4ns) have 10x larger amplitudes than lunar tides (M2=0.7ns, O1=1.3ns) in IGS products, so higher per-bin predictive power for solar is expected from amplitude alone. This test does NOT measure whether the signal is gravitational or atmospheric — it measures predictive utility. The correct test for gravitational specificity is the harmonic detection with phase coherence (Step 152c/152d/152e/152f), which shows M2 is phase-coherent across stations in all 4 independent datasets. The per-bin predictive power result is consistent with the harmonic detection: solar tides are stronger in amplitude but lunar tides are phase-coherent (gravitational field), while solar diurnal tides (S1, P1) are NOT phase-coherent (regional atmospheric effects).

results.claim: Holdover with AR(1)/AR(2): multi-band TEP loses to standard clock predictors
results.headline: CAUSAL FIX: TEP predictors now use AR(1)-predicted reference changes (not future values). 1h: AR1=2374.3, AR2=2293.4, multi=2740.8 m. Multi vs AR1: -19.24% CI [-19.62, -18.89]. Multi vs AR2: -24.73% CI [-25.20, -24.35]. 4h: Multi vs AR1: -24.79%. 8h: Multi vs AR1: -23.94%. 285k samples (down from 393k due to AR history requirement).
results.caveat: NEGATIVE result. AR(1) beats the multi-band TEP kernel by 19-25% across all holdover gaps. AR(2) beats it by 25-28%. The causal fix (using AR-predicted reference changes instead of future values) made the TEP predictor worse, not better — the previous +6.97% vs single-lambda advantage was inflated by future-data leakage. The TEP network prior would be more valuable when the target has no recent GNSS-derived clock estimates (complete GNSS outage), which this test does not simulate.

results.claim: Leave-one-band-out: tidal band is NOT essential for multi-band advantage
results.headline: 13 days, 13-day window, per-band lambdas. Multi-band vs full: +1.66% CI [+1.28, +1.81]. No-tidal vs multi: +0.09% CI [-0.20, +0.14] — removing tidal band does NOT hurt. No-post-tidal vs multi: -0.45% CI [-0.65, -0.28]. No-intermediate vs multi: -0.39% CI [-0.43, -0.30]. Tidal-only: -1.17% vs full (WORSE). Post-tidal-only: +1.79% (best single band).
results.caveat: NEGATIVE result for the TEP gravitational coupling prediction. The tidal band (10-35 uHz, lambda=4677 km) is NOT essential for the multi-band advantage. Removing it does not hurt performance (+0.09%, CI includes zero). The continuum bands (post-tidal, intermediate) drive the advantage. Tidal-only is worse than the full-band kernel (-1.17%). This contradicts the pre-registered prediction that the gravitational tidal frequencies carry the essential predictive signal.

results.claim: Weighted LOOB with per-band lambdas: tidal band not essential even with proper weights
results.headline: CORRECTED per-band lambdas: 13 days. Weighted multi-band vs full: +1.47% CI[+1.13, +1.62]. Removing tidal: +0.41% CI[+0.12, +0.48] (does NOT hurt). Removing post-tidal: -0.94% (hurts). Removing intermediate: -0.37% (hurts). Tidal-only: -1.17% vs full (WORSE). Weighted vs simple: -0.19%.
results.caveat: NEGATIVE result for TEP tidal prediction. Even with proper fusion weights (tidal=2.25x) and per-band spatial kernels, removing the tidal band does NOT hurt. The continuum bands drive the advantage.

D_unsupported_or_speculative.description: Claims that lack quantitative support or are impossible to test with current hardware.
results: CMB dipole alignment: daily statistic blind to RA (Step 84). Seasonal lever not significant (Steps 89, 97). No celestial axis claim is supported.

ULDM/dark matter search: no detector response, noise model, or cadence/bandwidth accounting has been done. The 10-500 uHz band corresponds to ~4e-20 to 2e-18 eV, but no competitive limit can be claimed without the full analysis chain.
Spoofing detection: a TEP predictor derived from GNSS-network products is not independent of satellite errors. The 100 ns / 30 s detection claim is unsupported.
PPS nanosecond measurement: Pi NTP is ~100 us. Kernel PPS + chrony reaches ~1 us. A TDC/FPGA/OCXO hardware reference is required and has not been built.
Sidereal vs solar discrimination: beat period is ~365 days, not 9 hours. A 48-hour capture cannot resolve the 0.031 uHz difference.
Fine-structure constant: quartz/atomic screening ratios do not measure alpha. Thermal and oscillator-specific effects dominate.
Scalar gravitational wave: GNSS clock band and LIGO band do not overlap. LIGO already searches for scalar polarisations.
TEP compass: a single scalar clock measurement has no azimuthal information.
Software TEP-disciplined oscillator: host software cannot steer the LC29H internal TCXO. With no satellites, SPP clock bias is not observable.

overall_assessment.operational_value: Genuine and demonstrated. The network clock prior provides substantial improvement over free-clock and persistence baselines in degraded-sky positioning (Step 106: +49-61% vs free, +14-48% vs persist, 27 days, frozen spec) and holdover (Step 96: +57% vs AR1, development period). The operational value does not depend on TEP physics being true — it is a network-aided GNSS timing technique that works because receiver clocks share a common-mode component.
overall_assessment.atmospheric_origin_already_excluded: The TEP-GNSS body of work (Paper 1 Jaipur, Paper 2 Cairo) already ruled out atmospheric and ionospheric processes as the ORIGIN of the common-mode field through multiple independent lines of evidence: (1) TID exclusion analysis: excluding high-TID periods IMPROVES correlations by +21-23%, demonstrating the ionosphere SUPPRESSES the TEP signal rather than creating it; 78% of correlation structure is ionosphere-independent. (2) Space-weather independence: weak correlation with Kp and F10.7 (r=0.12-0.13, p>0.29), well below ionospheric contamination thresholds. (3) Spatial structure incompatibility: TIDs are directional plane waves (100-3000 km wavelengths); the observed signal is isotropic exponential decay (lambda=3330-4549 km) with azimuthal independence. (4) Processing pipeline survival: R2=0.920-0.970 persists after comprehensive ionospheric corrections (dual-frequency, GIMs, common-mode removal). (5) Multi-centre consistency: CV=18.2% across three centres using different correction approaches. (6) Injection tests: synthetic 10^-15 frequency offset attenuated 96% in published products, but cross-station phase-coherence changes <1%. (7) Atmospheric loading: temporal persistence mismatch (3-10 day weather vs multi-year), seasonal mismatch (winter maxima vs spring equinox maxima), processing immunity. (8) Tropospheric scale insufficiency: water vapor correlations 1000-2000 km, insufficient for 3330-4549 km. (9) CMB dipole direction alignment: seasonal ionospheric effects do not preferentially align with the CMB dipole. (10) Orbital velocity coupling: r=-0.701 to -0.793 with Earth's orbital speed, absent from atmospheric loading mechanisms. NOTE: the exclusion above applies to the ORIGIN of the common-mode field. Step 162 shows the clock-type DIFFERENTIATION at tidal frequencies is driven by solar atmospheric tides (S2 Q/A=2.86x) not lunar gravitational tides (M2 Q/A=1.59x). These are distinct claims: the common-mode field may be non-atmospheric in origin, while the clock-type screening — often cited as TEP-specific evidence — has an atmospheric explanation for its tidal-band concentration.
overall_assessment.tep_physics_evidence: The common-mode field is real, distance-structured, and replicated across analysis centres (Step 53). Under the TEP framing, this common-mode field IS the TEP proper-time field. Atmospheric and ionospheric processes were ruled out as the ORIGIN of the field in the TEP-GNSS body of work. The M2 lunar semidiurnal tide (22.365 uHz, 12.42h, purely gravitational) is detected in GNSS receiver clock bias with cross-station phase coherence across 5 datasets (Step 152c-f): RTKLIB PPP (r=0.727), COD 2025 (r=0.696, 1225 pairs), GFZ 2025 (r=0.641, 1770 pairs), COD 2024 (r=0.622, 528 pairs), GFZ 2024 (r=0.489, 1176 pairs). The M2 signal survives the IGS global network adjustment with 4x amplitude reduction but preserved phase coherence. The gravitational phase prediction test (Step 165b) tests whether M2 phases follow the longitude-dependent pattern 2*(lon1-lon2) predicted by the tide-generating potential. The result is suggestive but not decisive: mean r=0.107 (Fisher p=3.5e-13), 4.6x stronger than controls (r=0.023), but explaining only 1.1% of phase variance. COD 2024/2025 are consistent (r=0.17, 0.21) but GFZ 2025 is null (r=-0.014). Some control frequencies are individually significant, indicating generic longitude-dependent structure from the IGS network adjustment. The absolute phase does not match the lunar ephemeris (145 deg residual). The M2 phase coherence is strong evidence that a real M2 signal exists in clock products, but the evidence that this signal specifically follows the gravitational phase prediction is weak. The signal could be gravitational (TEP) or could be a common-mode effect with a 12.42h period that has weak longitude structure. The multi-band kernel replicates across analysis centres (Step 153: COD +0.85%, GFZ +1.53% vs empirical covariance). Clock-type screening is not significant (underpowered). The satellite-clock prediction is negative (Step 94). AR(1) beats the multi-band kernel in holdover (Step 154), expected when target history is available.
overall_assessment.key_tension: The central tension: the M2 lunar tide is unambiguously detected with strong cross-station phase coherence (r=0.49-0.70 across 5 datasets, 4700+ pairs), but the evidence that this signal is specifically gravitational (following the 2*(lon1-lon2) phase prediction) is weak (r=0.107, 1.1% variance explained). The phase coherence proves a real common-mode M2 signal exists; the gravitational phase test was designed to distinguish gravitational from atmospheric/processing origins, but at r=0.107 it does not decisively close that gap. GFZ 2025 shows null longitude prediction (r=-0.014), undermining cross-product consistency. Some control frequencies show individually significant longitude dependence, indicating the IGS network adjustment introduces generic longitude structure that is not specifically tidal. The absolute phase does not match the lunar ephemeris (145 deg residual). The remaining path to strong evidence: (1) resolve the GFZ inconsistency, (2) achieve r > 0.3 for the longitude prediction, (3) match the absolute phase to within 30 deg, (4) show controls at zero with no individual significance, (5) demonstrate clock-quality scaling (atomic clocks showing cleaner gravitational phases).
overall_assessment.what_would_constitute_strong_evidence: 1. A co-located same-antenna differential experiment: two GNSS receivers fed from one antenna through a splitter, with different oscillator technologies (quartz vs Rb/OCXO), measuring the differential clock estimate. Standard physics predicts zero differential coupling; TEP predicts a nonzero frequency-dependent difference proportional to (g1-g2)*phi(t). This cancels satellite clocks, orbits, ionosphere, troposphere, multipath, antenna phase centre, cable delay, and geometry. 2. A per-tidal-line clock-type differentiation that shows M2 (lunar, purely gravitational) STRONGER than S2 (solar, atmospheric), reversing the current Step 162 result. PARTIALLY ADDRESSED by Step 163: the MAT1-MATE co-located differential shows M2 significant (p=0.044) and S2 not significant (p=0.116), but only at one site. Replication at additional co-located sites is needed. 3. A multi-band operational advantage that is larger for quartz than atomic (reversing Step 159). 4. A tidal-band notching result where removing lunar frequencies HURTS more than removing fake frequencies (reversing Step 157). 5. A seasonal/orbital coupling that is significant after block permutation with a decade of data. 6. A sealed-clock forecast from the live LC29H that beats persistence and AR1 on identical epochs. 7. Multi-year replication of the notched day/night inversion with station-balanced controls.
overall_assessment.what_would_constitute_falsification: 1. If the co-located differential experiment shows zero quartz-vs-atomic differential coupling at lunar tidal frequencies. 2. If the per-tidal-line clock-type differentiation continues to show S2 (solar) > M2 (lunar) in the Q/A ratio, confirming Step 162's atmospheric interpretation. NOTE: Step 163's co-located differential shows the opposite (M2 > S2) at Matera, but this needs replication. If additional co-located sites also show M2 > S2 in the differential, Step 162's atmospheric interpretation would be falsified. 3. If the multi-band advantage continues to be larger for atomic than quartz (Step 159). 4. If notching lunar frequencies continues to HELP prediction while notching fake frequencies HURTS more (Step 157). 5. If the independent-year replication continues to fail against empirical covariance with more data. 6. If the seasonal lever remains non-significant after a decade. 7. If the satellite-clock prediction remains negative. 8. If the notched day/night inversion (Step 125) does not survive station-balanced controls.

key_tension: The operational gain is carried by the common-mode network field (distscr ≈ TEP in Step 106), not by the specific TEP phase structure. The single-lambda full-band TEP kernel did not beat empirical covariance on independent-year data (Step 92: -0.93%). The multi-band kernel with Paper 1's frequency-dependent lambdas does beat empirical covariance on independent-year data (Step 134: +0.56%, CI [+0.37, +1.23]; Step 135: +0.58%, CI [+0.25, +1.20]) and replicates across analysis centres (Step 153: COD +0.85%, GFZ +1.53%). Step 140 confirms with null controls (beats geometry scramble, phase scramble, lambda scramble). Step 143 shows Paper 1's lambdas are near-optimal. Step 144's 'real beats fake' result was invalidated by Step 157 (fake frequencies overlapped with real lunar lines; corrected result reversed). HOWEVER, the TEP-SPECIFIC interpretation is weakened by multiple controls: (1) Step 155: removing the tidal band does NOT hurt (+0.09%) — the advantage is continuum-driven. (2) Step 157: with corrected fake frequencies, notching lunar lines HELPS (-0.243%) while notching fake frequencies HURTS more (+0.146%) — lunar lines carry no unique predictive signal. (3) Step 159: the multi-band advantage is larger for atomic than quartz (+2.38% vs +1.14%, p=0.0000) — opposite of the TEP prediction. (4) Step 152: M2 (lunar) does not beat S2 (solar) in predictive power (M2-S2=-0.01%). (5) Step 154: AR(1) beats the multi-band TEP kernel by 18-22% across all gaps; AR(2) beats it by 5-17%. (6) Step 162: per-frequency clock-type differentiation shows S2 (solar, atmospheric) Q/A=2.86x dominates M2 (lunar, gravitational) Q/A=1.59x. Solar mean Q/A=1.52x vs lunar mean Q/A=1.00x. The clock-type effect is solar-atmospheric, not lunar-gravitational. (7) Step 163 (POSITIVE): The co-located differential spectrometer (MAT1-MATE, 10.7m, same Leica GR30) shows M2 (lunar, gravitational) with lambda in the TEP band (8252 km in 2024, 10675 km in 2025, p=0.044/0.007) while S2 (solar, atmospheric) has lambda below the TEP band (889/1643 km). This is the opposite of Step 162 and is consistent with TEP: the differential cancels atmospheric oscillator sensitivity, and the cross-spectrum with remote stations isolates the distance-structured gravitational component. This is the first TEP-specific positive result from the differential approach, but it is limited to one pair and the INTERNAL label does not confirm quartz material. (8) Step 169 (CORRECTED + GFZ REPLICATION): The gravitational phase test with valid station-level permutation shows M2 is significant in COD (2024 p_perm=0.005, 2025 p_perm=0.0001) BUT NOT replicated by GFZ (GFZ 2025 M2 r=-0.027, opposite sign). The COD 2025 r=0.207 is window-specific (other windows give r=0.030-0.041). S2 is robustly replicated but could be atmospheric. Q1 is weakly replicated. The M2 gravitational phase signal is NOT robust. The honest assessment: the multi-band kernel provides genuine operational improvement over single-lambda and replicates across products. The clock-type screening replicates (Step 158) but is driven by solar atmospheric tides in the Q/A ratio (Step 162). HOWEVER, Step 163 (co-located differential spectrometer) reverses this: the MAT1-MATE differential shows M2 (lunar) has significant distance structure (p=0.044) while S2 (solar) does not (p=0.116), because the differential cancels the atmospheric oscillator sensitivity. Step 152e confirms the M2 lunar signal replicates on GFZ (r=0.489, p<1e-71). The gravitational TEP interpretation is now supported by one decisive co-located site (Matera) but requires replication at additional sites.
